title: Spring Security Essentials for Spring Boot Developers

cards.title: Introduction to Spring Security
cards.content:
Spring Security is a powerful, highly customizable framework for authentication and access control in Java applications.

Key concepts include:

  • Authentication: Verifying who a user is ("Who are you?").
  • Authorization: Determining whether a user is allowed to perform an action ("What can you do?").

cards.title: The Security Filter Chain
cards.content:
Spring Security is built on top of Servlet Filters. Every HTTP request passes through a chain of filters before reaching your controller.

Request -> Filter 1 -> Filter 2 -> SecurityFilterChain -> Controller

Common filters in the chain include UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter, BearerTokenAuthenticationFilter, and ExceptionTranslationFilter.

cards.title: Configuring SecurityFilterChain in Spring Boot 3
cards.content:
In Spring Boot 3, security is configured using a bean definition of type SecurityFilterChain rather than extending legacy adapter classes.

@Configuration
@EnableWebSecurity
public class SecurityConfig {

    @Bean
    public SecurityFilterChain filterChain(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
        http
            .authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
                .requestMatchers("/public/**").permitAll()
                .anyRequest().authenticated()
            )
            .formLogin(Customizer.withDefaults());
        return http.build();
    }
}

cards.title: Password Hashing with PasswordEncoder
cards.content:
Passwords must never be stored in plain text. Spring Security provides the PasswordEncoder interface for one-way password hashing.

The recommended implementation is BCryptPasswordEncoder, which uses the BCrypt strong hashing function with salt.

@Bean
public PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder() {
    return new BCryptPasswordEncoder();
}

cards.title: Loading Users via UserDetailsService
cards.content:
To load user-specific data during authentication, implement the UserDetailsService interface and override its single method:

@Service
public class CustomUserDetailsService implements UserDetailsService {

    @Override
    public UserDetails loadUserByUsername(String username) throws UsernameNotFoundException {
        // Load user from database or external source
        return new User(user.getUsername(), user.getPassword(), authorities);
    }
}

cards.title: Method-Level Authorization
cards.content:
You can secure individual service methods using annotations. Enable method security on a configuration class with @EnableMethodSecurity.

@Service
public class DocumentService {

    @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")
    public void deleteDocument(Long id) {
        // Admin only operation
    }
}
